title: Derived direct images of external coefficients with an acyclic first factor
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ and $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ be morphisms. Suppose $X$ is quasi-compact and $f$ has affine diagonal. Let $F$ and $G$ be quasi-coherent modules on $X$ and $Y$, respectively [pqf-def-coherent], and suppose $H^p(X,F)=0$ for every $p>0$ [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Put $E=\operatorname{pr}_1^*F\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*G$ on $X\times_kY$ [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations], and write $R^q\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}E$ for the module right-derived direct image [pqf-def-cohomology]. Then $R^q\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}E=0$ for every $q>0$, and there are a small set $I$ and morphisms $\iota_i:G\to R^0\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}E$ exhibiting $R^0\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}E$ as the coproduct of the constant family $(G)_{i\in I}$ in the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. No quasi-compactness, affine-diagonal, or cohomological acyclicity hypothesis is imposed on $Y$ or $G$.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover of X using its quasi-compactness. Affine diagonal implies affine finite intersections. For each affine open V of Y, cover X times V by U_i times V. The affine fibre-product, pullback-section and tensor-section comparisons identify each term with the finite product of F(U_intersection) tensor_k G(V). The pure-tensor formulas commute with restrictions and identify the Cech differential as d tensor 1.

Every vector space over k is flat. Exact tensor preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology of the Cech complex; finite products commute with tensor. Affine Cech comparison identifies the result with H^p(X,F) tensor_k G(V). Thus positive cohomology on X times V vanishes by hF, and degree zero is Gamma(X,F) tensor_k G(V). All identifications commute with restrictions in the affine basis.

Apply the higher-direct-image presheaf comparison on the affine basis. Its sheafification universal property and stalk isomorphisms identify positive direct images with the zero sheaf and the zeroth direct image with the sheafification of V maps to Gamma(X,F) tensor_k G(V). Choose a k-basis of Gamma(X,F). Its basis expansion identifies this tensor presheaf with the presheaf coproduct of copies of G. Sheafification is a left adjoint, hence carries this coproduct cofan to a coproduct cofan of module sheaves. Transfer it through the zeroth-direct-image isomorphism. The basis is not assumed finite; when Gamma(X,F)=0 the indexing set is empty. The argument also applies to empty X or Y and zero G.

theorem picardExternalCupCoefficients_directImages
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal f)]
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p →
      IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F)) :
    (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q →
      IsZero (((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage
        (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived q).obj
          (externalCupCoefficients f g F G))) ∧
    ∃ (I : Type w)
      (ι : ∀ _ : I, G ⟶ ((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage
        (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived 0).obj
          (externalCupCoefficients f g F G)),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk _ ι))
